neet_phy_u14_t00_1.working: ΔΦ per turn = 4 − 1 = 3 mWb. |e| = NΔΦ/Δt = 100 × 3×10⁻³ / 0.02 = 15 V.

neet_phy_u14_t00_2.working: dΦ/dt = (6t − 2)×10⁻³ Wb/s, which is 10×10⁻³ Wb/s at t = 2 s. |e| = N dΦ/dt = 20 × 0.01 = 0.2 V.

neet_phy_u14_t00_3.working: Initial flux per turn = BA = 0.4 × 0.05 = 0.02 Wb; final flux = 0 (plane parallel to field). |e| = NΔΦ/Δt = 200 × 0.02 / 0.5 = 8 V.

neet_phy_u14_t00_4.working: A coil at rest in a steady field has no change in flux, so no emf is induced: A is false. Induced emf depends on the rate of change of flux, not on the flux itself: R is true.

neet_phy_u14_t00_5.working: e = −dΦ/dt = Φ₀ω sin ωt, which is zero when cos ωt = ±1, i.e. when flux is maximum: I is correct. An emf is induced in an open coil even though no current flows: II is correct.
